_comment: Cross-desk subject vocabulary for Indo-Pacific Record.
This is separate from desks/china/taxonomy.json topical_labels, which are the legacy China analysis categories already stored in article_categories.
No legacy category is renamed, reinterpreted, or automatically mapped by this file.
Assignments are multi-label and evidence-bearing. Version 1 defines vocabulary only; it does not classify any record.

groups.description: Military activity, posture, access, and operational competition.
Intergovernmental and military relationships, agreements, and cooperative activity.
Acquisition, industrial capacity, strategic capabilities, and enabling technologies.
Geographically bounded security questions that recur across multiple desks.
Economic instruments, supply chains, and controls with security implications.
Formal or semi-formal concepts about strategy, doctrine, force employment, and planning.

topics.description: Exercises, drills, training events, readiness activity, and combined or joint training.
topics.scope_note: Use for an identifiable training or exercise event. Routine operations without a training purpose belong elsewhere.

topics.description: Deployments, rotations, access arrangements, bases, ports, facilities, and persistent force posture.
topics.scope_note: Use when the location, duration, access, or distribution of forces is substantively at issue.

topics.description: Naval and maritime security activity, sea-lane protection, maritime domain awareness, and maritime incidents.
topics.scope_note: Geographic disputes may also receive a flashpoint topic. Coast-guard or coercive gray-zone activity may also receive gray_zone_coast_guard.

topics.description: Coast-guard operations, maritime law-enforcement coercion, militia activity, and sub-threshold military pressure.
topics.scope_note: Use for coercive or security-relevant activity below conventional armed conflict; do not apply to routine civilian enforcement without a security dimension.

topics.description: Defense-ministry, military-to-military, senior-official, and institutional diplomatic engagement.
topics.scope_note: Use for substantive defense or military engagement. Ceremonial contact alone is insufficient unless it records an official defense relationship.

topics.description: Alliance commitments, defense agreements, security partnerships, access frameworks, and recurring cooperative mechanisms.
topics.scope_note: Use when the durable relationship or formal framework is itself substantive, not merely because two countries appear in the same record.

topics.description: Purchases, tenders, acquisition programs, deliveries, upgrades, sustainment decisions, and capability procurement.
topics.scope_note: Use for a concrete acquisition or sustainment action. Broad industrial policy belongs under defense_industry.

topics.description: Defense production, industrial-base capacity, co-production, shipbuilding, munitions capacity, and defense-sector investment.
topics.scope_note: Use when production capacity, firms, industrial policy, or manufacturing is substantively discussed.

topics.description: Artificial intelligence, autonomy, quantum, advanced sensing, uncrewed systems, and other emerging defense technologies.
topics.scope_note: Apply only when the technology is materially part of the record, not for generic modernization language.

topics.description: Nuclear forces, nuclear posture, extended deterrence, strategic weapons, and nuclear command or signaling.
topics.scope_note: Use for nuclear-specific capability, posture, policy, or signaling.

topics.description: Cyber operations, information warfare, influence operations, electronic warfare, and information-domain capabilities.
topics.scope_note: Use for security-relevant cyber or information activity; routine public communications do not qualify.

topics.description: Military and security space systems, counterspace activity, space-domain awareness, launches, and space cooperation.
topics.scope_note: Use when space capability or security is substantive rather than incidental.

topics.description: Cross-strait security, Taiwan-related military posture, coercion, deterrence, and contingency planning.
topics.scope_note: This regional topic is distinct from the China Desk's legacy category slug taiwan; no automatic equivalence is implied.

topics.description: Security activity, disputes, operations, coercion, and defense policy tied materially to the South China Sea.
topics.scope_note: Use only when the South China Sea is a substantive subject, not merely a geographic transit reference.

topics.description: Security activity, disputes, operations, and defense policy tied materially to the East China Sea.
topics.scope_note: Use only when the East China Sea is a substantive subject.

topics.description: Economic policy explicitly linked to national security, resilience, strategic dependency, or defense preparedness.
topics.scope_note: Use for security-linked economic policy. Ordinary trade or macroeconomic policy is out of scope.

topics.description: Export controls, sanctions, investment restrictions, technology controls, and related coercive economic measures.
topics.scope_note: Use when the control or restriction itself is a substantive subject.

topics.description: Critical minerals, strategic materials, defense-relevant supply chains, stockpiles, and industrial resilience.
topics.scope_note: Use when the material or supply-chain issue is explicitly strategic, defense-related, or security-relevant.

topics.description: Doctrine, strategic concepts, operational concepts, force-employment theory, and formal strategic planning.
topics.scope_note: Use for substantive ideas about how force or state power should be organized or employed, not for routine policy announcements.
